items.title: Can a Food Forest Help Protect Farmers’ Crops?
items.description: Help the project restore more habitat by donating. See the pinned comment in the comments section. Could growing more food for wildlife help protect farmers’ crops? In Sumatra, Indonesia, the Orangutan Information Center is testing a food forest buffer between wild habitat and farmland. A space where people and wildlife can both find food. The idea is simple: plant abundant food for animals near the forest, with the hope that they’ll be less likely to visit farmers’ gardens. People can harvest from that shared forest too, while more protected growing areas help safeguard their crops. It’s an approach that takes both wildlife conservation and farmers’ livelihoods seriously. Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. #OrangutanConservation #Sumatra #ForestRestoration #Permaculture #Agroforestry

items.title: The KEY to Growing Trees in Drylands
items.description: Curious about designing with trees and water? Explore Oregon State University’s permaculture class, see the pinned comment in the comments section. Where do you start when growing trees in a dry landscape? With places that collect water. Rainwater-harvesting basins concentrate storm runoff. Tough native pioneer trees can then help create shade, shelter, and better conditions for other plants to grow. That’s the sequence: collect water, establish hardy trees, and build on the shelter they create. Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. #Permaculture #FoodForest #Agroforestry #TropicalGardening #LandRestoration

items.title: Cutting Trees to Save the Orangutan
items.description: Help the project restore more habitat by donating. See the pinned comment in the comments section. Cutting down trees to help save orangutans? In this case, the trees are oil palms. The goal is to bring back a diverse forest. In Sumatra, Indonesia, the Orangutan Information Centre has turned a former palm oil plantation into a permaculture food forest. The felled palms become compost, helping make way for new growth. The Centre’s founder, Panut Hadisiswoyo, says that within two years of the conversion, tigers, sun bears, and wild orangutans were visiting the site. The lesson isn’t simply “palm oil is bad.” It’s that protecting wildlife means protecting and restoring the diverse forests they depend on. Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. #OrangutanConservation #Sumatra #ForestRestoration #Permaculture #Agroforestry

items.title: How to Grow a Food Jungle in the Tropics
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. A food garden can grow in layers. In the wet tropics, a multi-story “food jungle” combines productive palms, trees that help build fertility, and fruit and nut crops below. The key is leaving room for sunlight. Space upper trees so light reaches the plants beneath, and use edges or clearings for crops that need more. Curious about designing with trees? Explore Oregon State University’s permaculture class, see the pinned comment in the comments section! #Permaculture #FoodForest #Agroforestry #TropicalGardening #LandRestoration

items.title: What If Every Skyscraper Became a Farm?
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. What if we treated every high-rise building like a little mountain and extended the ground upward? Singapore imports nearly all of its food, but it already has an incredible foundation for urban agriculture: 🏙️ Buildings capable of supporting greenery equal to 200% of their footprint 🌿 Approximately 2,000 hectares of green rooftop space 🍊 The potential to replace ornamental plants with productive species The infrastructure is already there. With permaculture design, the “green city” could become an edible green city. Could this work where you live? #Permaculture #FoodForest #UrbanFarming #RooftopGarden #Singapore

items.title: A Food Forest on the 51st Floor!
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. A food forest… on the 51st floor of a skyscraper. In the middle of Singapore, this rooftop farm grows fruit trees, shrubs, herbs, vines, edible flowers, and even attracts pollinating bees. Instead of planting a single layer of vegetables, this garden produces food vertically. It’s proof that even the most unlikely urban spaces can become productive ecosystems. What unused space in your city could be growing food? #Permaculture #FoodForest #UrbanFarming #RooftopGarden #Singapore

items.title: The Asphalt Was 127°F! Now This Street Is Cooling Down.
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. This water-harvesting basin was nearly 30°F cooler than the exposed asphalt beside it. In Tucson, streets, pavement, and buildings absorb heat all day, creating hotter and hotter urban environments. But when stormwater is redirected into planted basins, the street starts to change. Water soaks into the soil.Native trees grow.Shade returns.The ground cools down.And the neighborhood becomes more livable. This project is showing a real, practical solution to the urban heat island effect. One curb cut, one basin, and one street at a time. #EarthRepair #Permaculture #RegenerativeDesign #WaterHarvesting

items.title: Free Food On Public Land!?
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. This is free food growing on public land. In Tucson Arizona, stormwater that used to disappear down the street is now being redirected into planted basins, growing native food trees, edible flowers, mesquite pods, wolfberries, cactus fruit, and habitat for wildlife. It’s not just beautifying the neighborhood. It’s cooling the streets, rebuilding the soil, supporting native species, and creating real food security right outside people’s doors. This is what happens when a city stops wasting rainwater and starts growing life with it. #EarthRepair #RainwaterHarvesting #Permaculture #FoodForest #RegenerativeDesign

items.title: Breaking the Law to Save the Rain
items.description: Watch the full video on Andrew’s YouTube channel by clicking the related video link at the bottom of this video. This Arizona neighborhood used to be a sun-baked urban desert. Then the community started capturing the rain that was already flowing down their streets. Cutting curbs, building basins, planting native food trees, and turning public land into a living system. What started as an illegal curb cut became a model for cooling streets, growing food, recharging groundwater, and bringing life back into the city. Now the goal is to help this work spread even further. #EarthRepair #RainwaterHarvesting #Permaculture #RegenerativeDesign #FoodForest
